subject: Computer Networking
title: Li-Fi: Internet Through Light
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Li-Fi: Internet Through Light.

hook.text: What if your ceiling light also delivered internet? Li-Fi transmits data using visible light instead of radio waves.

buildup.text: LEDs flicker billions of times per second — too fast for your eyes but fast enough to encode data.

discovery.text: Li-Fi offers massive bandwidth without radio interference. Ideal for hospitals, aircraft, and dense indoor spaces.

twist.text: Light can't pass through walls. That's actually a security advantage — your signal stays contained in the room.

climax.text: Li-Fi remains experimental. Real deployments are rare, but lab speeds have exceeded 100 Gbps.

punchline.text: Li-Fi: where every light is a potential access point.

quiz.question: What medium does Li-Fi use to transmit data?

details.summary: Li-Fi transmits data using modulated visible light from LED fixtures, achieving speeds up to several gigabits per second. Light signals do not pass through walls, providing inherent security and zero interference with radio systems.
details.whyItMatters: Li-Fi offers a complementary wireless technology for environments where radio-based systems face interference, security, or spectrum limitations, expanding the wireless toolkit beyond radio waves.
takeaways: LED lights modulate too fast for eyes to see, carrying data
Light cannot pass through walls, providing physical security
Ideal for RF-restricted environments like hospitals and aircraft

faq.question: How can light carry data without visible flickering?
faq.answer: LED lights modulate their intensity millions of times per second. Human eyes cannot perceive changes faster than a few hundred hertz, so the light appears constant and steady. A photodetector in the receiving device reads these rapid intensity changes and decodes them back into digital data.

faq.question: Will Li-Fi replace Wi-Fi?
faq.answer: Li-Fi will complement Wi-Fi, not replace it. Light cannot pass through walls, so each room needs its own Li-Fi fixture. It only works with line-of-sight or reflected light. Wi-Fi's ability to penetrate walls and cover large areas makes it essential.
